forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran publicly announce a signed interim Hormuz commercial-shipping framework agreement before EOD 2026-08-19?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assessment: Oman channel reached an 'advanced stage' August 4-6 with geographic corridor coordinates circulating between parties (Axios, 5 Aug; Al Jazeera, 6 Aug; CNN, 4 Aug). But on August 8 Araghchi stated a reopening is 'subject to other conditions' including US redress for alleged MOU violations (CNN, 8 Aug). On August 10 Trump publicly demanded unspecified 'compensation' from Iran before talks can advance (CNN, 10 Aug) — a new condition absent from earlier drafts. Iran's parliament is simultaneously reviewing a competing 10-point framework with US/Israeli vessel bans and a 5-7% cargo levy, stricter than the Oman corridor draft (GlobalSecurity Day 161, 7 Aug). Three conditions must converge within 7 days for YES: (1) US drops or redefines the compensation demand; (2) Iranian parliament does not adopt the rival harder draft; (3) Oman or Iran MFA issues a signed-text readout. Historical base rate for 'near-deal' claims in this conflict converting to a signed instrument within 7 days: low. p=0.25.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a publicly confirmed signed interim framework agreement on Hormuz commercial shipping transit is announced by both the US and Iranian governments (or their named principals/representatives) before EOD 2026-08-19. A joint statement or named mediator (Oman FM, Qatar FM) announcement of a signed and mutually acknowledged text qualifies. Unilateral US or Iranian declarations of deal terms without the other side's public confirmation do NOT qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Axios/Al Jazeera) plus either US State Dept or Iranian MFA/IRNA confirming the same instrument.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreed-in-principle or 'framework agreed' announcements without a signed text = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran parliament passes the rival 10-point proposal without US acceptance = NO. If one side announces and the other denies within 24h, treat as NO unless clarified by both parties.

indicators.name: Oman FM readout confirming signed Hormuz text with named US and Iranian co-signatures
Trump publicly withdraws or substantially redefines the Aug 10 compensation demand
Iran MFA confirms acceptance of Oman-channel corridor text without additional pre-conditions

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed formally convened US-Iran negotiating session (direct or Oman/Qatar/Pakistan-mediated) occur before EOD 2026-08-26?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assessment: Qatar FM confirmed August 4 that the region is 'fully engaged' but no direct talks are scheduled (Euronews, 4 Aug). Oman's role as primary channel has expanded in recent weeks (CNN, 4 Aug). However, Iran's new national security chief — an IRGC veteran appointed around August 10-11 to replace the official previously associated with Hormuz framework negotiations — made public statements before appointment expressing skepticism toward formal US-Iran talks (US News/NBC, 7 Aug). Trump's August 10 compensation demand and Iran's August 8 MOU-violation claim add pre-conditions absent from earlier session frameworks. The last formally convened round: Islamabad talks, April 11-12 (Wikipedia 2025-2026 Iran-US Negotiations). Oman channel is relaying draft texts, not hosting formal sessions. p=0.35 reflects active mediator engagement against structural friction from both sides.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US principals (Witkoff or equivalent) and named Iranian principals (Araghchi or equivalent), hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Qatar/Pakistan), before EOD 2026-08-26.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/CNN/Al Jazeera plus confirmation from either US State Dept or Iran MFA/IRNA of the same session.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Relay of written messages, draft texts, or corridor coordinates through intermediaries without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Unilateral assertion of 'ongoing talks' without mediator or counterpart confirmation = NO.

indicators.name: Oman FM convenes named session with US and Iranian envoys and issues a readout
Iran new national security chief publicly endorses formal engagement in Oman-channel talks
Trump publicly withdraws the August 10 compensation demand

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz commercial transit volume reach >=40 vessels/day (7-day moving average) before EOD 2026-09-30?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assessment: Lloyd's List Intelligence (5 Aug) recorded 84 commercial transits July 27-August 2 = approximately 12 per day. Pre-crisis baseline was approximately 94 per day. Reaching >=40 per day within 49 days requires: (1) a signed Hormuz framework removing Iranian maritime friction; (2) MCM progress sufficient to support JMIC downgrade from SUBSTANTIAL to MODERATE and enable Lloyd's P&I war-risk cover reinstatement; (3) commercial operators willing to reroute from Cape of Good Hope to Hormuz. Even if F1 resolves YES by August 19, MCM timeline with degraded US assets (Avenger-class retired, LCS/drones in first operational deployment) realistically requires 4-8 additional weeks for a verified cleared corridor. JMIC's SEVERE-to-SUBSTANTIAL downgrade (August 5) is the first movement but remains far from MODERATE, the threshold at which shipping return normally accelerates. p=0.25 reflects the stacked dependencies against the tight timeline.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch or equivalent AIS aggregator (MarineTraffic, Lloyd's List Intelligence, Bloomberg shipping) records >=40 commercial vessel transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-09-30.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Lloyd's List Intelligence Hormuz Brief plus one of: IMF PortWatch, Bloomberg shipping data, or Reuters/AP/AFP shipping report confirming the same 7-day average.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Military or naval vessels do not count toward commercial transit total. Navy-escorted commercial convoys count as commercial transits. If PortWatch is unavailable, use best AIS source and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources diverge by more than 20%. Isolated single-day surges without a qualifying 7-day rolling average = NO.

indicators.name: Lloyd's List records 7-day average of >=25 transits/day (leading indicator toward 40)
JMIC downgrades Hormuz threat level from SUBSTANTIAL to MODERATE
Lloyd's P&I war-risk cover reinstated for Hormuz commercial transit

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran publicly sign a comprehensive peace/nuclear framework agreement covering nuclear enrichment limits, Hormuz freedom of navigation, and a sanctions roadmap before EOD 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assessment: The June 17 MOU established a 60-day framework that broke down in early July when Iran struck commercial vessels (Arms Control Association, July 2026). Current Hormuz talks are an intermediate step; a comprehensive agreement requires resolution of enrichment caps, sanctions architecture, Hormuz governance, and reconstruction financing ($300B MOU incentive now disputed). New pre-conditions from both sides (US compensation demand, August 10; Iran MOU-violation claim, August 8) have stalled even the intermediate step. Mediators (Qatar, Oman, Pakistan) remain active and describe a 'comprehensive deal' as the stated end goal. Israel's October 27 election creates a partial Trump political incentive to demonstrate diplomatic progress before year-end. Against this: Iran's new IRGC-veteran national security chief; Iran parliament's competing harder framework; US weapons inventory attrition (senior US commanders cited 80% depletion of key interceptors) creates leverage pressure but also inflexibility. p=0.25.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a publicly confirmed signed comprehensive agreement is jointly announced by the US and Iranian governments, covering all three domains: (1) Iran nuclear enrichment limits or elimination; (2) Hormuz freedom of navigation guarantee; (3) US sanctions relief roadmap — before EOD 2026-10-27.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept and Iran MFA/IRNA joint or simultaneous announcement plus two TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN) confirming all three domains are covered.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Hormuz-only interim deal without nuclear or sanctions elements = NO. Nuclear-only deal without Hormuz = NO. Agreed-in-principle without a signed text = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. MOU extension or renewal without new nuclear commitments = NO.

indicators.name: F2 (formal US-Iran session by Aug 26) resolves YES
F1 (Hormuz interim deal signed) resolves YES and holds for >=2 weeks without new Iranian attacks on commercial shipping
Iran formally accepts zero-enrichment or cap-enrichment as negotiating basis in named-official statement

forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. The June 17 MOU was executed as a remote asynchronous instrument — Trump in Washington, Pezeshkian in Tehran — without a formally convened held session before EOD June 16. Araghchi stated June 3 that 'no formal negotiation process is underway — only written messages are being exchanged' (CNN, Times of Israel). Ambiguity rule triggered: written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. No Iranian MFA or IRNA statement rescinding the June 1 suspension was issued before June 16. The MOU signing on June 17 — one day after the deadline — does not retroactively satisfy the June 16 horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Iranian MFA spokesman confirms re-engagement or rescinds suspension
Omani/Qatari mediator readout of a convened/held session

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed convened US-Iran negotiating session occur before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. The June 17, 2026 MOU constitutes a formally concluded instrument between named US and Iranian principals (Witkoff/Kushner and Araghchi/Pezeshkian), facilitated via Oman and Pakistan mediation, within the June 10-24 forecast window. Military Times, CNN, and Arab Center DC each published the full 14-point text. Both governments independently confirmed the same instrument — qualitatively distinct from mere message relay and meeting the 'formally convened' criterion. The signing occurred within the forecast window (June 17 < June 24).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar), between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Al Jazeera/Times of Israel; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Mere relay of written messages, or one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: TIER1 report of a convened session
Iran MFA statement lifting the June 1 suspension

forecasts.question: Will a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both ways) occur in any 48h window before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. CNN live-blog (June 7-8): 'Ceasefire falters as Israel and Iran trade worst strikes in months' — confirmed bilateral exchange within the forecast window. Britannica (2026 Iran war) confirms large-scale two-way fighting continued through the June 17 MOU signing, with both IDF and IRGC strikes documented. Arms Control Association (July 2026) documents continued bidirectional exchange around the MOU period. Israeli strikes on Iranian targets and Iranian strikes on Israeli/claimed targets within the June 10-17 sub-window confirmed by two independent TIER1 sources (CNN; Britannica/Arms Control Association cross-reference). 48h rolling window criterion met.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Proxy-only attacks (Hezbollah/Houthi) without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do NOT count; one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IDF + IRGC reciprocal strike statements within 48h
TIER1 confirmation of two-way strikes in a single window

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Lloyd's List Intelligence (August 5 brief) documented July 27-August 2 transits at approximately 12 per day — the highest since the crisis began but far below 50 per day. No seven-day rolling average of >=50 commercial transits was recorded before EOD July 2. Britannica confirms transit 'stayed well below normal' after the June 17 MOU opening. MCM bottleneck, war-risk insurance gaps, and Iran's July 6-7 attacks on commercial vessels (occurring after the July 2 deadline, but confirming the transit environment was not sustainably open) together precluded threshold attainment.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

Al Jazeera (June 25) published a full visual explainer of 'How minesweeping in the Strait of Hormuz works,' providing TIER1 confirmation within the June 10-July 10 forecast window that operations were actively underway. Operations commenced April 11 — well before the July 10 deadline.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Knesset third and final reading of the dissolution bill: July 17, 2026 (Haaretz, Times of Israel, JNS, Al Jazeera confirm the 62-0 vote). Election date set to October 27 in a coalition meeting on July 12 (Times of Israel). Both resolution conditions unmet: (1) final vote occurred July 17 — two days after the July 15 EOD deadline; (2) election date is October 27 — the constitutional maximum, not 'earlier than 2026-10-27' as required. The forecast's hygiene was demonstrated by exactly capturing the edge case: the dissolution happened, but two days late and to the maximum-date election.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

indicators.name: Plenum third-reading dissolution vote held with a fixed date inserted

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Knesset voted 62-0 on July 17, 2026 to dissolve parliament; Netanyahu cast a vote in favor (Haaretz, Times of Israel, JNS). Election date confirmed as October 27 — the mandatory constitutional maximum, not earlier. The coalition maintained 61+ seats throughout the parliamentary term; no coalition partner formally departed before the dissolution vote. Neither YES condition was met: (1) no coalition majority loss — the dissolution was a planned unanimous vote, not a confidence failure; (2) election date equals the mandatory Oct 27 date, not 'earlier than 2026-10-27.' The NO condition in resolution criteria is met: 'coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.' Resolved as of July 17, 2026. Note: DA recommended RESOLVED-YES on grounds Netanyahu 'announced early dissolution' — Judge rejects this; the dissolution was for the mandatory constitutional date, and the YES condition explicitly requires election date 'earlier than 2026-10-27,' which was not satisfied.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.
